md_docs_2keyboard-input(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2keyboard-input(3)

NAME

md_docs_2keyboard-input - Keyboard input

Native keyboard input has four boundaries:

  • lib/platform/{posix,windows}/keyboard.c owns terminal/console access and restoration.
  • lib/platform/keyboard.c frames terminal escape sequences and replies, buffers fragmented text and delegates UTF-8 decoding, scalar validation, and encoding to utf8proc. Windows UTF-16 surrogate pairs become the same normalized keys; console repeats apply to complete characters.
  • lib/tui/input.c collects bracketed paste and queues decoded events in order. The media screen supplies the policy for recognizing dropped path/URL bursts. Paste bytes are validated before insertion and never execute shortcuts.
  • lib/ui/input.c edits caller-owned UTF-8 storage without terminal I/O or rendering. Prompts and log search share this implementation; callers decide when to submit, cancel, mask, or insert newlines. lib/tui/input.c retains screen ownership and modal routing, and shortcuts.c owns shortcut aliases/help.

Text and control keys use their Unicode code points directly. Special keys start at 0x110000, above the Unicode range, so no text tagging is needed. The browser SessionUi adapter uses the same representation, including supplementary characters. Bracketed POSIX paste payloads remain bytes until whole-paste validation. Malformed and truncated typed sequences cannot mutate a field; new starters or special keys discard incomplete text. Buffer exhaustion rejects a whole inserted character or paste without truncating it.

Editing operates on Unicode code points. Combining marks and emoji joiners remain valid UTF-8 but are separate editing units; this is not grapheme-cluster editing.

Validation

The normal Criterion suites exercise the production library with the configured sanitizers: platform keyboard text/editing, UI text editing/event collection, terminal replies, log search, and UTF-8 utilities. The password PTY regression also types and deletes accented characters, CJK, and supplementary emoji.

On a configured Linux/macOS Clang build with Criterion and pkg-config, run:

python tests/scripts/keyboard_text_coverage.py --build build

This runs the same exhaustive Criterion tests for every non-NUL Unicode scalar, malformed UTF-8, fragmented input, and UTF-16 recovery. It requires 100% line and branch coverage of the three keyboard_text_* Unicode functions in lib/platform/keyboard.c and writes its counters, gcov listing, and summary under the sibling build-keyboard-text-coverage/ directory. The focused measurement excludes sanitizer-generated branches and vendored utf8proc internals; the ordinary integrated tests retain sanitizers. This percentage does not describe all Unicode utilities or the whole application.
